answer: The wharf multiplier is published, charged in canyon, and ridge lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4805 identities would post 848 proofs and burn roughly 12 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
